target.title: fix(browser): bound Chrome launch stderr diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where users could hit Chrome launch failures or stuck startup with OpenClaw retaining the entire launch stderr stream in memory before the final diagnostic slice was applied.
- Affected surface / workflow: Managed Chrome startup in `extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.ts`, specifically the launch path that waits for Chrome CDP readiness and includes stderr diagnostics when startup fails.
- Root cause, in product terms: During launch, OpenClaw attached a stderr listener to the Chrome child process and appended every emitted chunk into an unbounded `Buffer[]`. The code only redacted and sliced stderr after CDP startup failed, so a noisy or stuck Chrome process could grow OpenClaw memory usage before the timeout/error path was reached.
- Why it matters / User impact: Chrome startup failures should provide useful diagnostics without making the parent OpenClaw process vulnerable to unbounded memory growth from stderr. Users still need the recent Chrome failure output, but they should not pay memory cost for arbitrarily large historical stderr that will never be displayed in full.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Fix classification: Root-cause bounded-buffer fix with regression coverage. This caps stderr retention at the collection boundary instead of only changing final error-message formatting.
- Complete shipped solution: The launch path now stores stderr in a bounded 64 KiB tail while waiting for CDP readiness. On failure, that bounded tail is converted to text, passed through the existing `redactToolPayloadText` path, displayed with the existing `CHROME_STDERR_HINT_MAX_CHARS` slice, and passed to existing Chrome launch hint detection. The listener is still detached and the retained buffer is cleared when the launch attempt exits.
- Why this is root-cause fix: The memory growth source was the pre-failure collection point, not the final error-message formatting. Bounding the retained bytes at append time caps memory while preserving the existing redaction, display, and hinting contracts downstream.
- Key design boundary / source of truth: The source of truth remains the Chrome launch diagnostic path in `launchOpenClawChrome`. This patch only changes how much stderr that path retains during startup; it does not change CDP readiness probing, browser selection, redaction policy, or the `CHROME_STDERR_HINT_MAX_CHARS` display limit.
- Non-goals / what did not change: This does not change Chrome launch arguments, retry behavior, singleton-lock recovery, CDP diagnostics, or long-running Chrome stderr handling after a successful launch. It also does not expand the user-facing diagnostic size; the existing displayed hint cap is preserved.
- Compatibility, merge-risk, or maintainer-decision notes: Availability risk considered because this touches Chrome startup failure diagnostics. The behavior change is intentionally limited to retained stderr history during launch failure; Chrome process startup, CDP probing, retry/recovery, and final redaction/display limits are unchanged.
- Risk labels considered: `merge-risk:availability` was considered because browser launch diagnostics are part of the availability/debuggability path.
- Risk explanation: The main diagnostic tradeoff is that very old stderr may be omitted once output exceeds 64 KiB. Recent stderr is retained because it is usually the actionable startup failure context, and retaining all historical stderr was the memory hazard.
- Why acceptable: The fix caps memory at the collection boundary while preserving the existing user-visible diagnostic pipeline and adding targeted regression coverage for the large-stderr failure mode.

## User Impact

- Users/operators/developers can now: Hit Chrome launch failures or stuck startup cases with a bounded stderr retention footprint while still seeing recent stderr diagnostics in the failure message.
- Existing behavior preserved: Failure messages still include redacted stderr when available, still cap the displayed hint with `CHROME_STDERR_HINT_MAX_CHARS`, and still use the same launch-hint logic for sandbox/display/profile-in-use guidance.
- What was not tested or remains unavailable: I did not run a real Chrome binary startup proof in this environment. The regression uses the existing mocked Chrome launch harness to deterministically emit large stderr before CDP failure and verify the retained diagnostic tail behavior.

## Evidence

- Environment: Windows Git Bash worktree, Node v22.17.0 / pnpm v11.2.2. pnpm emitted the repo's Node engine warning (`>=22.19.0 <23 || >=23.11.0`) but the targeted checks below completed successfully.
- Commands run after this patch:
  - `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.internal.test.ts --passWithNoTests=false --reporter=verbose -t "stderr"`
  - `pnpm exec oxfmt --check extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.internal.test.ts`
  - `pnpm exec oxlint extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.internal.test.ts --deny-warnings`
  - `git diff --check`
- Key results / observations: Targeted Vitest stderr coverage passed with 3 passed and 52 skipped; formatter check passed on both modified files; Oxlint passed on both modified files with denied warnings; `git diff --check` passed. `origin/main` still has `const stderrChunks: Buffer[] = []` and `Buffer.concat(stderrChunks)`, and does not have `CHROME_LAUNCH_STDERR_TAIL_MAX_BYTES` or `createBoundedBufferTail`. Open PR duplicate check found no open PR touching `extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.ts` in the latest open PR listing, and searches for `chrome stderr`, `launchOpenClawChrome stderr`, and `bounded stderr tail` returned no matches.
- Review findings addressed, if any: No existing PR review findings; this is a new direct fix for the reported daily-fix item.
- Regression guardrail: Added a launch failure test that emits an old stderr marker followed by more than the bounded tail size of recent stderr, then verifies the failure message keeps recent diagnostics, drops the old marker, remains within the existing display cap, and kills the failed fake Chrome process.
- Patch quality notes: The production change is limited to one source file and one test file. The added test `catch` captures the expected launch error message for assertion; the added fixture `return true` / `return false` values are scoped to mocked `fs.existsSync` path control and do not affect production behavior.
- Maintainer-ready confidence: Medium-high. The diff is focused, the risky behavior is covered by a deterministic unit test, and validation covers the affected stderr diagnostics path plus formatting/lint/whitespace checks. Confidence is not marked higher only because this environment did not run a real Chrome launch proof.
